description: The image displays a series of five unscaled bar charts illustrating different distribution patterns or shapes. The horizontal axis serves as a baseline for the categories, which are labeled below each respective chart as "Increasing", "Uniform", "Decreasing", "Spindle", and "Bottleneck". There is no vertical value axis, scale, tick marks, or units provided, meaning the heights of the bars represent relative, unquantified values. Each of the five labeled categories consists of a group of four adjacent bars. All bars share a uniform visual style, featuring a light greenish-grey fill with a subtle speckled texture and solid black outlines. In the "Increasing" chart, the four bars progressively increase in height from left to right, starting with the shortest and ending with the tallest. Conversely, the "Decreasing" chart features bars that progressively decrease in height from left to right. The "Uniform" chart contains four bars of identical height. The "Spindle" chart displays a symmetrical pattern where the two outer bars are short and the two inner bars are tall. Finally, the "Bottleneck" chart shows the opposite symmetrical arrangement, with two tall outer bars and two short inner bars. The charts are arranged horizontally from left to right, and no specific bars are visually emphasized beyond their structural height differences.
